text.arabic_uthmani: وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ أَلَيْسَ هَٰذَا بِٱلْحَقِّ ۖ قَالُوا۟ بَلَىٰ وَرَبِّنَا ۚ قَالَ فَذُوقُوا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive connector carrying the previous resurrection proof into the judgment scene

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the ayah joined to the previous proof about reviving the dead (46:33). The connector turns the new Day-scene into consequence: proven power becomes enacted judgment, and the prefixed sound binds the boundary to {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) rather than letting the scene start in isolation.

topics.headline: resumptive bridge into judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the scene continues the resurrection-capacity proof of 46:33 instead of opening as a detached episode.
topics.reason: The rows converge on resumption, coordination, and boundary linkage; local grammar permits the opening particle to connect 46:34 backward while launching the temporal scene.

words.gloss_range: accusative temporal frame for the eschatological trial scene
words.root_gloss_range: bounded time, decisive day, or epoch; here narrowed to the judgment frame rather than ordinary daylight
words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) is accusative as a temporal frame, with an implied act of remembering or a prior discourse governor. Though unarticleed, the surrounding Fire, truth question, confession, and sentence specify it as the known judgment Day. Its singular form compresses the four-beat trial sequence into one bounded epoch, while links to 46:20 and the parallel exposure formula at 40:46 show the scene as a recognized eschatological pattern.

topics.headline: bounded judgment-day frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one time-word frames the whole exposure, question, confession, and sentence as a single judgment event.
topics.reason: The rows on case, implied governance, singular compression, eschatological valence, and same-surah/cross-surah echoes cohere with the QAC temporal-adverb analysis.

words.gloss_range: Form IV passive presentation/exposure in an unfolding courtroom scene
words.root_gloss_range: presenting, displaying, exposing, opposing, and breadth; here narrowed to compelled exposure before the Fire

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:يُعْرَضُ}} ({{tr:yuʿraḍu}}) is imperfect passive: the presenter is suppressed and the exposed group becomes the visible patient-subject. The root field of presenting, displaying, and breadth survives locally as forced exposure before {{ar:ٱلنَّارِ}} ({{tr:al-nār}}), while the active turning-away branch is only a contrast: the passive form makes avoidance become confrontation. The phrase also echoes exposure-before-Fire language in 46:20 and 40:46, with this ayah compressing that exposure formula into a courtroom interrogation.

topics.headline: passive exposure before the Fire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deniers are not merely mentioned; they are made visible before the Fire in a passive exposure that reverses concealment.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support IV passive with the relative group as passive subject and the Fire phrase as complement; broader root branches are kept only where they sharpen the local exposure scene.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun making the deniers the passive subject and defining them by their act

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) serves as the passive subject of {{ar:يُعْرَضُ}} ({{tr:yuʿraḍu}}) and opens the defining clause {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}). The grammar first places them under exposure, then lets the following verb name the charge that defines the class. That delay makes their identity legal and deed-based.

topics.headline: relative identity as defendant class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accused are identified by the clause of denial, not by lineage or any independent group label.
topics.reason: The rows are supported by the local passive-subject attachment and by the relative clause that defines the group through the following denial verb.

words.gloss_range: perfect plural denial without an explicit object, defining the accused and opening a root ring
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealing, ingratitude, and theological denial; here selected as completed culpable denial with covering imagery retained

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) is perfect plural and has no explicit object, so the relative clause identifies the group by completed denial without narrowing what was denied. The covering image of the root remains useful because the next major action is exposure: what was covered is answered by being displayed. The same root later closes the ayah in {{ar:تَكْفُرُونَ}} ({{tr:takfurūna}}), shifting from third-person identity to second-person habitual charge.

topics.headline: opening completed denial frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening charge is both completed and unrestricted, then returns at the end as direct habitual accusation.
topics.reason: The perfect form, omitted object, relative-clause role, and closing root echo are all locally licensed; broader root imagery is narrowed to the covering/denial pressure relevant to exposure and verdict.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the Fire as the before/against endpoint of presentation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) governs {{ar:ٱلنَّارِ}} ({{tr:al-nār}}) with {{ar:يُعْرَضُ}} ({{tr:yuʿraḍu}}), making the Fire the endpoint and facing-place of exposure. Its spatial “upon/before” force and adversarial “against” pressure converge, so the accused are presented before the Fire as the object of confrontation.

topics.headline: preposition of confrontational presentation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the presentation is not neutral display; the preposition directs it toward an adversarial Fire-confrontation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the prepositional phrase the complement of the passive presentation verb; the adversarial nuance is preserved as local pressure, not as a separate parse.

words.gloss_range: definite eschatological Fire governed by the presentation phrase
words.root_gloss_range: fire and light in the n-w-r field; here narrowed to destructive Fire, with light contrast only as background

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّارِ}} ({{tr:al-nār}}) is definite, genitive after {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}), and functions as the endpoint of exposure. The form names the known eschatological Fire, not generic fire, and supplies the visible referent that {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) can point toward. The broader {{ar:ن و ر}} ({{tr:n-w-r}}) field includes light, but the local selection is destructive Fire; any light/fire antithesis remains a narrowed background contrast.

topics.headline: known Fire as visible endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Fire is the known scene-anchor that makes the following “this” visible and unavoidable.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence fix the word as definite prepositional complement; V4 range supports narrowing the n-w-r field to the local Fire sense.

words.gloss_range: interrogative plus negation verb forming a compelled truth-verification question
words.root_gloss_range: negation through the defective verb “laysa”; here converted by interrogation into forced affirmation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
local phrase cited in the prose for grammatical context
nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:أَلَيْسَ}} ({{tr:a-laysa}}) combines interrogative hamza with the defective negation verb. It governs {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) as subject and {{ar:بِٱلْحَقِّ}} ({{tr:bi-l-ḥaqqi}}) as predicate, but the question is rhetorical: the negated form pressures the defendants into the affirmative answer {{ar:بَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:balā}}). The speaker remains unidentified in the grammar, so the force belongs to the courtroom exchange rather than to a named human questioner.

topics.headline: negative question forcing affirmation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the courtroom question uses negation to compel acknowledgment rather than to seek information.
topics.reason: Local syntax confirms the laysa clause and the following answer confirms the interrogative as taqrīrī, while rows about speaker identity remain bounded by the unspecified subject.

words.gloss_range: proximal demonstrative serving as the subject of the truth question

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) is the subject of {{ar:أَلَيْسَ}} ({{tr:a-laysa}}) and turns the proof into deixis: “this” is now present before the accused. The referent is intentionally broad within the local scene, able to include the Fire, the punishment, and the whole eschatological display. That breadth makes the truth-predicate inclusive rather than vague.

topics.headline: proximal deictic evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that abstract denial is answered by something pointed to as present: Fire, punishment, or the whole judgment scene.
topics.reason: QAC marks the demonstrative as ism of laysa and notes referent ambiguity; the rows are narrowed to local deictic breadth, not an unlimited referent.

words.gloss_range: pleonastic or reinforcing bāʾ in the predicate of laysa

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) attaches to {{ar:ٱلْحَقِّ}} ({{tr:al-ḥaqqi}}) as the reinforced predicate of {{ar:أَلَيْسَ}} ({{tr:a-laysa}}). Here the particle is not causal; it intensifies predication in the negated question. Its later counterpart at word 20 has a different function, turning the repeated particle shape into a movement from verified truth to assigned cause.

topics.headline: reinforcing truth-predicate bāʾ
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first bāʾ strengthens the truth-predicate, while the second bāʾ later introduces the cause of punishment.
topics.reason: QAC identifies this bāʾ as reinforcing in the khabar of laysa, while the second bāʾ is causal; the repeated-form topic survives as contrastive function.

words.gloss_range: definite truth/reality/right predicate asserted of the visible scene
words.root_gloss_range: truth, reality, right, firmness, and obligation; here all converge in the predicate “the Real”

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَقِّ}} ({{tr:al-ḥaqqi}}) is the predicate of the laysa clause, reinforced by {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}). The definite gerund turns truth into a substantive reality: what is visible is true, right, real, and binding. The word also draws same-surah pressure from 46:30, where guidance to the truth becomes, here, indictment by the truth.

topics.headline: the Real as courtroom predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question does not ask whether the scene is merely true; it asks whether this visible judgment is the established Real with moral claim.
topics.reason: The grammar supports predicate identity, and the root range is narrowed to the local truth/reality/right convergence rather than a divine-name reading controlling the parse.

words.gloss_range: perfect plural speech verb introducing the defendants’ direct answer
words.root_gloss_range: saying, utterance, and reported speech; here direct collective confession

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: local phrase cited in the prose for grammatical context
nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) introduces the direct answer {{ar:بَلَىٰ وَرَبِّنَا}} ({{tr:balā wa-rabbinā}}). Its perfect plural form makes the future judgment speech narratively certain and collective, and it turns the exposed group from displayed defendants into speakers of their own confession. The later singular {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) answers their plural speech with authoritative sentence.

topics.headline: collective confession speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that exposure turns into testimony: the same deniers now speak the admission demanded by the question.
topics.reason: The rows on direct speech, plural subject, narrative certainty, and qālū/qāla contrast match the local sequence of question, answer, and sentencing speech.

words.gloss_range: answer particle reversing the negative question into confession

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
local phrase cited in the prose for grammatical context

words.prose: {{ar:بَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:balā}}) answers {{ar:أَلَيْسَ}} ({{tr:a-laysa}}) with the required reversal of negation. It is not a casual yes; it converts the courtroom question into confession and then opens into oath reinforcement through {{ar:وَرَبِّنَا}} ({{tr:wa-rabbinā}}). The covenant-like echo with 7:172 is useful as a pattern of compelled affirmation, while the local scene remains judgment.

topics.headline: affirmation after negated question
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the confession is grammatically forced: the answer particle is the one used to affirm after a negative question.
topics.reason: QAC confirms balā as the response to a negative question; the covenant echo is retained as formulaic contrast and not allowed to override the local courtroom setting.

words.gloss_range: oath particle introducing the sworn appeal to “our Lord”

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) after {{ar:بَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:balā}}) functions as oath wāw, not ordinary coordination alone. It extends the answer into {{ar:رَبِّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbinā}}), making the confession sworn by the very Lordship relation that denial had refused.

topics.headline: oath wāw after confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the confession is reinforced by an oath in which the deniers invoke the Lord they had resisted.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as oath wāw governing the following Lord noun; the irony of acknowledgment is locally tied to the oath construction.

words.gloss_range: construct Lord noun with first-person plural suffix as the object of oath
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, mastery, nurture, and cultivation; here invoked as confessed Lordship in an oath

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbinā}}) is genitive as the sworn-by object after oath {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}). The construct form and first-person plural suffix make Lordship definite and claimed: the exposed speakers invoke “our Lord” after being defined by denial. The root range of authority, ownership, and nurturing relation survives as relational pressure, especially because the earlier second-person warning in 46:32 becomes their first-person claim at judgment.

topics.headline: our Lord as sworn witness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the defendants do not merely admit truth; they claim “our Lord” in the very moment of judgment.
topics.reason: The oath syntax, possessive suffix, and root-field rows all cohere; nurturing and ownership are retained as Lordship pressure without displacing the local oath function.

words.gloss_range: singular perfect speech verb introducing the command of sentence
words.root_gloss_range: saying and pronouncement; here authoritative sentencing speech

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) introduces the sentencing utterance after the defendants’ oath-confession. The subject is grammatically singular and unnamed, so the ayah highlights the authority of the pronouncement more than the identity label of the speaker. The shift from plural {{ar:قَالُوا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) to singular {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) makes many voices answerable to one decisive command.

topics.headline: singular sentencing speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the authority shift: many confessing voices receive one singular sentencing voice.
topics.reason: QAC supports a 3ms perfect verb with unspecified subject governing direct speech; rows naming possible speakers are preserved only as bounded uncertainty.

words.gloss_range: consequential fāʾ linking confession directly to punishment command

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the imperative clause consequential. After the confession, it pivots immediately into {{ar:ذُوقُوا۟}} ({{tr:dhūqū}}), so acknowledgment does not open negotiation; it triggers sentence. The particle’s force is causal and sequential at once.

topics.headline: zero-gap consequence particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that confession and sentence are grammatically adjacent: the command follows as consequence without delay.
topics.reason: QAC allows explanatory or causal fāʾ before the command; the CRITICAL rows converge on immediate confession-to-sentence linkage.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural imperative commanding the defendants to taste the punishment
words.root_gloss_range: tasting, sensory contact, and intimate experience; here punishment made bodily and undeniable

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:ذُوقُوا۟}} ({{tr:dhūqū}}) is a second-person plural imperative taking {{ar:ٱلْعَذَابَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿadhāba}}) as its direct object. The taste root makes the sentence bodily and undeniable: those who denied now must experience what they had refused to recognize. The command belongs to a recurring punishment formula, including 8:35, 32:14, 34:46, 39:24, and 46:34, but its local function is the courtroom verdict after confession.

topics.headline: taste command as bodily sentence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that punishment is ordered as firsthand experience, not merely announced as information.
topics.reason: QAC verifies imperative 2mp and direct-object syntax; formula rows and root semantics are locally integrated as sentencing, not invitation.

words.gloss_range: definite direct object of the taste command
words.root_gloss_range: punishment/torment with an older sweetness contrast; here narrowed to the known punishment object

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
local phrase cited in the prose for grammatical context

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَذَابَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿadhāba}}) is definite and accusative as the object of {{ar:ذُوقُوا۟}} ({{tr:dhūqū}}). It is not generic suffering but the known punishment already threaded through the surah, now made the tasted object of sentence. The root’s sweetness/torment contrast remains a narrowed lexical background; the local sense is punishment, placed before {{ar:بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ}} ({{tr:bi-mā kuntum takfurūna}}) so the sentence lands before its cause is named.

topics.headline: known punishment as tasted object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command’s object is the known punishment itself, placed before the clause that states its cause.
topics.reason: The direct-object grammar and definite form are decisive; contronym rows are retained only as root-level color, not as an alternate local sense.

words.gloss_range: causal preposition governing the final reason phrase

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: local phrase cited in the prose for grammatical context

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) in {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bi-mā}}) governs the following clause as cause. Unlike the reinforcing {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) at word 10, this particle assigns the reason for the punishment: the sentence is because of the sustained disbelief named in the final clause. The repeated particle shape maps truth-predicate into causal verdict.

topics.headline: causal bāʾ after verified truth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the particle chain: the first bāʾ reinforces what is true, and this second bāʾ states why punishment follows.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the second bāʾ as causal over the following mā-clause; contrast with word 10 is a locally licensed structural payoff.

words.gloss_range: relative or maṣdar-like particle making the following disbelief clause a causal noun

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
local phrase cited in the prose for grammatical context

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) receives the causal scope of {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) and makes {{ar:كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ}} ({{tr:kuntum takfurūna}}) function as the noun-like cause. It may be read relatively, “what you denied,” or maṣdar-like, “your denying”; both readings keep the clause under causal scope and broaden the reason rather than weakening it.

topics.headline: mā nominalizes the cause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cause is grammatically internal to the sentence, compressed into a single “because of what/your denying” clause.
topics.reason: QAC allows mā maṣdariyya or mawṣūla; both parse options serve the same local function as formal cause after the causal bāʾ.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural kāna auxiliary making the final denial a sustained past state
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, existing, and formation; here narrowed to auxiliary past-state force

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:كُنْتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) functions as defective kāna with {{ar:تَكْفُرُونَ}} ({{tr:takfurūna}}) as its predicate. The kāna-plus-imperfect construction marks habitual past action, and after the earlier third-person narration the -tum ending keeps the sentenced group directly addressed after {{ar:ذُوقُوا۟}} ({{tr:dhūqū}}). The root field of being survives as narrowed pressure: their past existence is summarized as a state of continuous denial.

topics.headline: habitual past state of denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final accusation is not a single act report; the auxiliary makes denial their sustained past state.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support kāna auxiliary grammar; existential rows are narrowed to auxiliary state-description rather than treated as an independent lexical predicate.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural imperfect denial closing the ayah as the legal cause
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealing, ingratitude, and theological denial; here persistent covering-denial under kāna

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word cited in the prose for local context
nearby word cited in the prose for local context

words.prose: {{ar:تَكْفُرُونَ}} ({{tr:takfurūna}}) is the imperfect predicate under {{ar:كُنْتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}), so the final charge is habitual past denial. It has no explicit object, keeping the denial broad, and its second-person plural ending leaves the defendants addressed as “you.” The root returns from opening {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) to close the ayah: third-person completed identity becomes second-person ongoing cause.

topics.headline: closing habitual denial charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends not on punishment but on the sustained denial that explains punishment.
topics.reason: The imperfect predicate, object omission, direct-address ending, and k-f-r ring are all supported by local grammar and row evidence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The passive presentation at word 2, the two K-F-R occurrences at words 4 and 18, the fire at word 6, and the truth question at words 7-9.
baseline_models.mechanism: Covering is reversed by forced visibility: the coverers are brought before sight at a kindled fire, and the reality they had obscured is converted into an admitted fact.

activation_trace.role: Presentation as bringing something before sight supplies the scene's public disclosure operation.
The covering image supplies what the presentation reverses: agents of concealment are themselves uncovered.
Kindled fire supplies the literal destination while also making the exposure visually inescapable.
Truth as stable correspondence names what forced sight and compelled speech now have to match.

changed_reading.before: A straightforward scene in which unbelievers are shown the fire and acknowledge that it is real.
changed_reading.after: A reversal of concealment in which the people defined by covering are publicly uncovered, and their speech is forced to coincide with visible reality.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The negative interrogative at words 7-9, the paired speech occurrences at words 10 and 13, the lordship oath at word 12, and the imperative sentence at words 14-15.
baseline_models.mechanism: The question is not a request for information. It stages a contested claim, obtains an oath-backed admission before the sovereign, and turns the answering exchange directly into an executable sentence.

activation_trace.role: The frozen negation, reinforced by the following construction, frames a confirmation question rather than open uncertainty.
The branch of opposed parties claiming right supplies the adversarial shape of the truth question.
Speech as an exchange over an affair makes the two utterances an on-record proceeding, not loose conversation.
Lordship as ownership and sovereignty gives the oath its authority and locates the sentence under rightful rule.
Truth as an obligation that has become due lets admission pass immediately into deserved consequence.

changed_reading.before: The condemned are asked whether the fire is true and then are punished.
changed_reading.after: The exchange is a compact ratification procedure: confrontation, oath-backed admission, and sentence form one judicial act.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The taste imperative at word 14, punishment at word 15, the past-state construction at word 17, and the repeated K-F-R root at words 4 and 18.
baseline_models.mechanism: Verbal denial is answered in the register of direct testing. What would not be admitted as knowledge becomes bodily experience, while the past-state construction binds that experience to an enduring practice of occlusion.

activation_trace.role: Tasting as testing and undergoing makes punishment compulsory first-person knowledge.
Painful penalty supplies the concrete content of the experience rather than leaving tasting metaphorically empty.
Being or occurring through time makes the causal charge a sustained former condition, not a single lapse.
Blocking acknowledged truth names the epistemic failure that direct experience now closes.

changed_reading.before: Tasting is an idiom for suffering a penalty caused by disbelief.
changed_reading.after: The penalty is also an epistemic conversion: denied truth becomes unavoidable bodily knowledge, causally matched to a settled habit of denial.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier agentive turning-away from warning is reversed into passive presentation before the fire. The same root changes who controls orientation: first they turn their side away; finally they are placed before what they avoided.

activation_trace.role: Turning one's side away supplies the earlier self-directed movement of avoidance.
Warning that should awaken caution identifies what the earlier turning deliberately leaves behind.
Being brought forward for sight supplies the terminal, externally controlled orientation.
Covering links avoidance of the warning to the identity of those now exposed.

structural_cues: The same root appears at the close of 46:3 in an agentive turning-away form and at the opening of 46:34 in a passive presentation form.
Warning precedes avoidance; forced encounter follows it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the shared root, opposing grammatical orientations, and ordered warning-to-judgment sequence; I infer that chosen avoidance matures into loss of control over orientation. A live alternative is simple lexical contrast without a strict causal equivalence.

changed_reading.before: The focus presents the condemned for inspection.
changed_reading.after: Their presentation is the exact reversal of their prior posture: those who kept turning away are made unable to turn away.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier speech assigns a deceptive label to truth when it arrives; the focus repeats the speech-truth-demonstrative complex but removes their power to rename. Their final utterance must match the reality before them.

activation_trace.role: Overtly pronounced speech supplies the earlier public act of classification.
Stable reality supplies the object that their earlier label fails to match.
Deceptive diversion supplies the false classification imposed on the arriving truth.
Pronounced speech now records acknowledgment instead of strategic relabeling.
Truth as correspondence makes the final answer linguistically fit what is shown.

structural_cues: Both scenes join speech, the truth term, and a proximal demonstrative.
The earlier scene speaks upon arrival of clear signs; the focus speaks after presentation to the fire.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opposite labels attached to a repeated speech-truth frame; I infer a correction from discretionary naming to compelled matching. The focus truth term could alternatively refer only to the immediate fire, leaving the earlier mislabeling as a looser echo.

changed_reading.before: The final answer acknowledges an evident fact.
changed_reading.after: The answer repairs a long-standing speech act: the mouth that renamed truth as deception is finally made to name reality without substitution.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier lord-confession is followed by sustained uprightness and safety, while the focus contains an oath to the same lord followed by punishment. The contrast relocates efficacy from bare wording to confession embodied before exposure and maintained through time.

activation_trace.role: Speech as held belief makes the earlier confession a lived position rather than a momentary answer.
Lordship supplies the shared relational claim across the saving confession and the final oath.
Upright steadiness supplies the durable enactment that follows and validates the earlier confession.
The same lordship relation appears in the final oath, but only after exposure.
Immediate undergoing marks the outcome of a confession that arrives without prior steadfast embodiment.

structural_cues: Both scenes put a first-person plural possessive relation to the Lord inside direct speech.
In 46:13 upright continuance follows confession; in 46:34 the tasting command follows confession.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated lord-confession and sharply different sequels; I infer that timing plus sustained enactment distinguishes saving acknowledgment from evidentiary acknowledgment. A live alternative is rhetorical contrast rather than a formal criterion of efficacy.

changed_reading.before: Invoking the Lord intensifies the sincerity of the condemned's admission.
changed_reading.after: The oath exposes the insufficiency of last-stage wording: the same relational vocabulary saves when lived in advance but only testifies when forced at judgment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier statement that a word has become due is enacted in the focus as a question-answer-command sequence, while the intervening promise of full payment supplies its distributive precision. Truth is both correspondence and an obligation reaching execution.

activation_trace.role: Becoming fixed and due supplies the legal force already attached to the coming word.
Speech functioning as judgment lets the due word operate as a verdict over its addressees.
Full delivery without deficiency supplies the exact settlement that the verdict must accomplish.
The truth term carries the earlier due obligation into the confirmation question.
The paired utterances stage the due word as an exchange that concludes in execution.

structural_cues: The assertion that the word became due in 46:18 precedes graded and complete repayment in 46:19.
The focus compresses confirmation and command into adjacent speech turns.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a due word, complete repayment, and a final dialogic command; I infer that the focus dramatizes the execution of that due word. The live alternative is that the earlier word denotes a general decree rather than this specific exchange.

changed_reading.before: The focus contains a truthful question followed by a punitive command.
changed_reading.after: The dialogue is the performative arrival of a previously due verdict, completed without underpayment or excess.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier parallel presentation scene sets consumed good things and worldly enjoyment against recompense on that day. The focus's taste imperative therefore closes a consumption-shaped exchange: prior taking-in is answered by compulsory undergoing.

activation_trace.role: Good and wholesome things supply the pleasant objects consumed before judgment.
Enjoyed benefit supplies the active worldly consumption side of the exchange.
Recompense as action matched by return supplies the directional bridge from enjoyment to penalty.
Direct tasting converts the returned consequence into a counter-experience the recipients cannot decline.

structural_cues: 46:20 and 46:34 open with the same day-presentation-to-fire sequence.
The earlier parallel names prior enjoyment and present recompense; the focus replaces that explanation with an imperative to taste.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a near-duplicate scene plus enjoyment, recompense, and tasting; I infer a consumption-to-counter-consumption arrow. The alternative is that tasting remains a conventional suffering idiom and the pleasure vocabulary only specifies conduct, not the penalty's form.

changed_reading.before: Tasting emphasizes the intensity of punishment.
changed_reading.after: Tasting also completes a retributive economy of consumption: unaccountable enjoyment is answered by an experience imposed on the enjoyer.

context_deltas.mechanism: A previously appearing cloud is read as promised rain but proves to carry painful punishment. The focus reuses the presentation root and then demands a truth judgment, turning the final scene into correction of a catastrophic visual misclassification.

activation_trace.role: Something appearing from a direction supplies the ambiguous visual object first classified as beneficent.
Rain falling from cloud supplies the observers' expected good outcome.
Punitive rain supplies the branch-level reversal latent inside the expected weather reading.
Painful penalty identifies the actual cargo of what had been welcomed as rain.
Formal presentation removes the earlier object's ambiguity by fixing the viewers before it.
Correspondence with reality is the perceptual judgment they can no longer get wrong.

structural_cues: Both scenes combine the A-R-D root with seeing or demonstrative identification and direct speech.
The earlier correction changes expected rain into punishment; the focus elicits an unqualified affirmative answer.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a failed visual classification and a later presentation followed by a truth question; I infer that the later encounter closes the gap between appearance and reality. The alternative is a local narrative echo with no general perceptual mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The focus makes the reality of punishment visually obvious.
changed_reading.after: It also retrains a perception that once converted danger into hoped-for benefit: this presentation cannot be redescribed as welcome rain.

context_deltas.mechanism: Hearing, sight, and hearts previously fail to benefit their owners because knowing denial overrides them, and the mocked consequence surrounds them. The focus converts those failed faculties into unavoidable exposure and taste: perception can no longer remain behaviorally inert.

activation_trace.role: Hearing as understanding and compliance supplies the benefit their auditory capacity failed to produce.
Inner sight supplies the discernment their repeated visual capacity failed to become.
Denial despite knowledge supplies the blockage between available perception and responsive action.
Descending harm that encloses its target supplies the transition from ignored signs to immersive consequence.
Direct undergoing completes the sensory circuit that hearing, sight, and inner response had left open.

structural_cues: 46:26 repeats each faculty first as a gift and then as something that did not avail.
The focus moves from being shown, to speaking, to tasting in a tightly ordered sensory sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed faculties, knowing denial, enclosing harm, and later compelled sensation; I infer that punishment forces perception to become consequential. The alternative is that the faculty list explains culpability while tasting merely describes penalty, without a designed sensory completion.

changed_reading.before: The condemned see the fire and then suffer it.
changed_reading.after: The scene completes a failed sensorium: capacities once detached from acknowledgment are replaced by sight, speech, and bodily experience that cannot be detached from truth.

context_deltas.mechanism: The call to answer once opened forgiveness and protection; refusal meant inability to escape and absence of protectors. The focus contains an answer at last, but after presentation, so response has changed function from a path of rescue into self-ratifying testimony.

activation_trace.role: Answering as returned speech supplies the response that was requested while rescue remained open.
Protective shelter within a binding relation supplies what timely response was offered against punishment.
The same returned-speech branch marks the response explicitly withheld in the next step.
Failure to outrun or escape supplies the consequence of nonresponse that presentation now realizes.
Protective alliance supplies the support explicitly absent when the nonresponders face consequence.
Overt speech supplies the eventual answer, now elicited inside judgment rather than invitation.

structural_cues: 46:31 commands an answer and couples it with forgiveness and protection from punishment.
46:32 defines the non-answerer by failed escape and absent allies; 46:34 then records an affirmative answer followed by punishment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an ordered answer-or-rescue offer, nonresponse consequences, and a later spoken answer; I infer that response remains semantically recognizable but loses saving efficacy after exposure. The alternative is that the final acknowledgment is courtroom testimony with no intended link to the earlier response verb.

changed_reading.before: The affirmative answer simply confirms the truth of the scene.
changed_reading.after: It is a tragically late response: the speech act once associated with rescue survives, but its timing converts it into evidence for the sentence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding ayah asks a negative question about divine capacity to revive the dead and supplies an affirmative answer. The focus repeats that interrogative-answer contour, but the affirmative now comes from the condemned, transferring a doctrinal answer into witnessed self-testimony.

activation_trace.role: Seeing with eye or insight supplies the evidence-request frame that precedes the first affirmative answer.
Effective capacity supplies the proposition affirmed immediately before the judgment scene.
Loss of life supplies the apparently impossible state against which capacity is affirmed.
Negative framing preserves the preceding question's confirmation-seeking contour.
Pronounced speech reassigns the affirmative response from narratorial proof to the defendants' own mouths.

structural_cues: Two consecutive ayat use a negative question followed by the same affirmative response token.
The first answer follows a proposition about reviving the dead; the second is spoken by those presented to the fire.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency and a repeated question-answer grammar; I infer deliberate reassignment of the correct answer to the defendants. The alternative is ordinary idiomatic repetition with no transfer of speaker role.

changed_reading.before: The condemned independently concede the truth when they see it.
changed_reading.after: Their concession echoes an answer already established one verse earlier, making their speech a forced entry into the surah's prior proof.

context_deltas.mechanism: The following instruction rejects haste and says that, on seeing what was promised, the judged will measure their prior stay as only an hour of a day. The focus day therefore operates less as a calendar unit than as the severe event that collapses the felt duration of delay.

activation_trace.role: Hastening and bringing forward supplies the rejected demand that judgment arrive sooner.
A span of time supplies the scale against which the earlier stay is retrospectively compressed.
Remaining in a place supplies the duration that collapses once the promised sight arrives.
The day as a severe happening makes the focus a threshold event whose intensity reorganizes remembered time.

structural_cues: The focus opens with the day of presentation; the next ayah returns to the day on which the promise is seen.
The post-focus sequence places non-hastening beside a retrospective stay measured as only an hour of daylight.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies delayed promise, seeing, and compressed retrospective duration; I infer that the focus event changes the condemned's scale of time. The alternative is that the comparison concerns worldly lifespan only and does not modify the semantic force of the focus day.

changed_reading.before: The opening day phrase locates the scene at a future date.
changed_reading.after: The day is also a temporal threshold: once it arrives, the long delay that enabled denial contracts to almost nothing in the condemned's own retrospect.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates neighboring branches of the punishment root involving abstention and withholding, rather than replacing the explicit penalty branch. It remains anchored in the adjacent taste-punishment construction and is strengthened by the earlier enjoyment scene. Downstream prose should present it as a lexical-material undertone of forced weaning or deprivation, not as the surface definition of punishment.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The immediate adjacency of tasting at word 14 and punishment at word 15, with the parallel enjoyment scene in 46:20.

activation_trace.role: Literal tasting of food supplies the material ingestion frame for the imperative.
A body refusing food and drink supplies deprivation as the paradoxical substance now tasted.
Withholding and weaning supplies the secondary action imposed after unrestricted enjoyment.
Prior enjoyment supplies the condition from which the final tasting can be imagined as forced weaning.

changed_reading.before: The imperative means only to undergo painful punishment.
changed_reading.after: As a contained undertone, the punishment is a counter-meal of deprivation: those habituated to enjoyment are forced to experience withholding itself.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a form-distant activation from the packet's secondary mapping of Q-W-L to Q-L-L, so it cannot govern the ordinary meaning of the two speech verbs. It remains anchored because both speech occurrences share that supplied split-root inventory and the scene is a forced reversal of settled denial. Downstream prose should mark trembling or instability as an acoustic-affective resonance, never as a lexical translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The two Q-W-L speech occurrences at words 10 and 13, especially the condemned's oath-backed answer under exposure.

activation_trace.role: A tremor caused by fear or anger supplies an affective vibration beneath the otherwise orderly dialogue.
Agitation and loss of stability supplies a secondary image of denial being shaken into admission.

changed_reading.before: The two speech turns form a controlled judicial exchange.
changed_reading.after: At an exploratory affective level, the repeated speech sites also carry instability: the admission sounds shaken loose from a position that can no longer hold.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the surface referent is plainly fire, while illumination and waymark branches add a secondary function that could be over-spiritualized. It remains anchored in the fire root, the act of public presentation, and the demand for truth recognition. Downstream prose should keep literal punishment primary and describe revelatory light or marking only as a concurrent function.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The fire at word 6 stands between public presentation at word 2 and compelled truth recognition at words 7-10.

activation_trace.role: Kindled fire preserves the literal punitive object that contains the secondary activation.
Illumination supplies the fire's concurrent capacity to make what was covered perceptually undeniable.
A visible waymark supplies the fire's role as a terminal sign that can no longer be passed without recognition.
Public display supplies the visual setting in which illumination and marking become functional.
Manifesting truth supplies the epistemic result of the fire's secondary revealing function.

changed_reading.before: The fire is solely the object and instrument of punishment.
changed_reading.after: Without ceasing to be punishment, the fire also functions as illumination and terminal marker: it reveals the truth that covering had kept from operative recognition.

strongest_changes: The A-R-D recurrence reverses voluntary turning-away into involuntary presentation.
The final answer is a belated response after the earlier forgiveness-and-protection window has closed.
The paired scenes in 46:20 and 46:34 turn tasting into a recompense structured by prior consumption and enjoyment.
The due word of 46:18 is plausibly enacted as the focus's question-answer-command sequence.
The immediately preceding negative question and affirmative answer are reassigned to the condemned in the focus.
summary.what_was_special: The focus concentrates reversals of agency, speech, perception, and consumption into one short scene: coverers are uncovered, misnamers speak matching truth, nonresponders finally answer, and failed perception becomes compulsory experience. Split-root and branch-distant cues preserve additional resonances of trembling speech, forced deprivation, and revealing fire without displacing the surface reading.
remaining_uncertainties: The causal arrow from earlier turning-away to later presentation is strongly patterned but still reader-supplied.
The final affirmative may echo 46:33 deliberately, or the repetition may be ordinary confirmation grammar.
The consumption and forced-weaning readings depend on material analogy and should remain secondary to explicit punishment.
The Q-W-L to Q-L-L tremor activation is packet-authorized but highly form-distant and must remain exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Presentation forces a truth-recognition formerly covered.** ع ر ض B002 is presenting to view; ك ف ر B003 is covering or rejecting truth, and ح ق ق B001 is firm truth against falsehood. The deniers are displayed before the fire and asked to identify reality. I infer that forced presentation removes the covering maintained in earlier life. Their `بلى` is therefore a compelled reversal from concealment to acknowledgment.
2. **Truth moves from proposition to tasted experience.** ذ و ق B002 is experiencing and testing something, alongside B001’s literal tasting. The dialogue first elicits verbal recognition, then commands `فذوقوا`. I infer that sensory experience enforces the truth just admitted in speech. The ayah reads as an escalation from statement to embodied verification, while preserving the concrete taste image.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 46:35 compresses the duration that deniers treated as impossible delay, making the presentation in 46:34 part of a reversed time-scale. The final command to convey also confirms that recognition was preceded by sufficient notice.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Presentation to fire turns rejected truth into an inspectable relation.** `يُعْرَضُ` activates ع ر ض B002, being brought forward for inspection; `كَفَرُوا` activates ك ف ر B001, covering, and B003, rejecting truth, while `ٱلنَّارِ` activates ن و ر B002, burning fire. The question `أَلَيْسَ هَذَا بِٱلْحَقِّ` activates ل ي س B001, emphatic present negation in the question, and ح ق ق B001, established truth. The packet makes the rejecters inspect what they had covered and asks them to identify its status. I infer that judgment discloses the relation denial had hidden: the truth is no longer discussed at a distance but presented with its consequence.

2. **Their own speech now confirms the authority their covering had refused.** `قَالُوا بَلَىٰ` activates ق و ل B001, spoken utterance; `رَبِّنَا` activates ر ب ب B001, authority and ownership, and the answering `قَالَ` keeps the exchange explicit. The packet records their affirmative answer and appeal to their Lord. I infer that compelled clarity reverses 46:32’s nonresponse and disclosed straying: the tongue now acknowledges the authoritative relation it had failed to answer. Speech finally states what covering had kept practically inactive.

3. **Punishment is made experiential as the matched consequence of continued rejection.** `فَذُوقُوا` activates ذ و ق B002, experiencing or undergoing a tested hardship; `ٱلْعَذَابَ` activates ع ذ ب B005, severe punishment, and the causal `بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ` reactivates ك ف ر B001/B003, sustained covering and rejection. The packet explicitly ties the experience to what they had been doing. I infer that “taste” closes the gap between abstract denial and embodied knowledge: what could be verbally covered becomes personally undergone. The command does not introduce a new issue but makes the rejected claim experiential.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 46:35 changes the scale of the presentation: when the promise is seen, prior staying through ل ب ث B001 seems only a small portion of the daylight span named by ن ه ر B002. That final compression sharpened 46:34’s forced truth-recognition as the sudden collapse of a delay that had seemed long enough to sustain covering.

baseline.text: İnkâr edenlerin ateşe sunulacağı gün onlara, “Bu gerçek değil mi?” denir. “Evet, Rabbimize andolsun” derler. “Öyleyse inkâr etmeniz yüzünden azabı tadın” der.

findings.text: Ateşin önünde zorla görünür kılınma, daha önce gerçeğin üstüne çekilen örtüyü kaldırır ve inkârı kişinin kendi sözüyle kabule çevirir.
Gerçek önce sözle kabul edilir, ardından tatma buyruğuyla bedende sınanan deneyime dönüşür; böylece soyut ret ile yaşanan bilgi arasındaki mesafe kapanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bilinen günü güneşin doğuşundan batışına kadar süren zaman olarak tanımlar ve onu günler dizisinin tek bir birimi sayar. Verilen dal çerçevesi bu iki kurucu özelliği de doğru biçimde korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal yalnızca sınırları gün doğumu ve gün batımıyla belirlenen gündüz süresini kapsar; belirsiz süre, devir ve olay anlamları ayrı dallardadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal yalın kullanımı tanımlar; günlük işlem bildiren türemiş kullanım, temel gün anlamının yerine geçirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Güneşin doğuşundan batışına kadar uzanan bilinen zaman aralığı ve bu aralıklardan oluşan dizinin tek bir birimidir.

facets.statement: Başlangıcı güneşin doğuşu, sonu güneşin batışıdır; aynı zamanda sayılabilen günlerden biridir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, bilinen günün güneşin doğuşuyla başlayıp batışıyla bittiği ve çoğulu bulunan sayılabilir bir zaman birimi olduğu konusunda birleşir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Günün geceyi dışarıda bırakan, doğal ışık sınırlarıyla belirlenmiş tek bir zaman birimi olarak kastedildiği kullanımlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Hem gün doğumu ile gün batımı arasındaki sınırı hem de tek bir gün birimi olmayı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Karşıtlığın geceyle kurulduğu ve sayılabilir birim özelliğinin bağlamdan zaten anlaşıldığı cümlelerde doğal bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Güneşin doğuşu ile batışı arasındaki aydınlık zaman aralığını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Hem doğal gündüz sınırının hem de bunun tek bir sayılabilir birim olduğunun açıkça belirtilmesi gereken bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Sınırlandırılmış gündüz süresini ve onun tek bir gün birimi oluşunu birlikte korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: gün gün veya gündelik esasa göre yapılan işlem

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Gün doğumunu kesin başlangıç sayar ve aralığı sayılabilir tek bir gün birimi olarak kurar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Gündüz ışığını ve şafaktan gün batımına uzanan süreyi kapsar; ayrıca gündüzle ilişkili başka kullanımları da içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de gecenin karşısındaki aydınlık zaman kesitini gün batımına kadar anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal, başlangıcı güneşin doğuşu olan sayılabilir günü tanımlar. Komşu dal ise şafaktan başlayan gündüzü ve onun ışığını öne çıkarır; bu yüzden sınırları tam örtüşmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Süreyi gün doğumu ile gün batımı arasında kesin olarak sınırlar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Her uzunluktaki bir zaman dilimini ve bazı bağlamlarda bir devri anlatabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir zaman kesitini gün sözü üzerinden kavramlaştırır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal doğal göksel sınırları olan bilinen gündür; komşu dalın süresi belirlenmemiştir ve devir kadar genişleyebilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Olayın niteliğinden bağımsız, gerçek bir gündüz zaman aralığını belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Büyük veya çetin bir olayı, onun yaşandığı kritik günü ya da çoğulda olayları belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Olay dalındaki kullanımlar, bir gün içinde yaşananlardan hareketle bu zaman birimiyle ilişki kurar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın çekirdeği zamansal sınırdır. Komşu dalda gün, olayın büyüklüğünü veya çetinliğini taşıyan mecazî ve bağlama bağlı bir anlatıma dönüşür.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; yalnızca gündüz sınırı, belirsiz süre ve olay günüyle doğrudan karışabilecek üç komşu yayımlandı.
branches.what_is_ar: اليوم المعروف: وقت من طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وهو الواحد من الأيام وجمعه أيام.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس المراد هنا مطلق الدهر، ولا الوقائع والنعم، ولا تركيب يومئذ.
branches.source_phrase_ar: اليوم: الواحد من الأيام (maqayis)؛ اليوم مقداره من طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها (ayn;tahdhib)؛ اليوم معروف والجمع أيام (sihah)؛ اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi sözü herhangi bir uzunluktaki zaman süresi için genişletir ve bazı kullanımlarda devir anlamına geldiğini açıkça belirtir. Dal çerçevesi, sınırlı gündüz anlamından bu geniş zamansal kullanıma geçişi doğru yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal, uzunluğu önceden belirlenmeyen süreyi ve bağlama bağlı devir anlamını kapsar; belirli gündüz aralığını veya olayın kendisini tanımlamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın biçimin belirsiz süre ve devir kullanımı, iki karşıt hayat durumunu anlatan özel söz öbeğinden ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Uzunluğu önceden sınırlandırılmamış bir zaman dilimidir; bazı bağlamlarda kişinin veya bir şeyin devri kadar geniş bir süreyi anlatır.

facets.statement: Herhangi bir uzunluktaki zaman süresini belirtir ve bilinen gündüz sınırlarına bağlı değildir.
Bağlama göre uzun bir devir veya bir varlığın yaşadığı dönemler anlamına genişleyebilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bu kullanımda gün sözünün sabit gündüz süresinden çıkarak herhangi bir zaman dilimini, özel bağlamlarda ise bir devri anlatabildiğini gösterir.

concept_gloss.text: herhangi bir zaman dilimi; bağlama göre devir
concept_gloss.applicability: Sürenin gün doğumu ve gün batımıyla sınırlandırılmadığı, kısa veya uzun bir dönem ya da bütün bir devir olarak yorumlandığı kullanımlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Hem süre uzunluğunun serbestliğini hem de bağlama bağlı devir genişlemesini korur.
